claim: The 'nothing is sent' guarantee lives only in a client-side wrapper around WahaClient (C1), but the real invariant is at the WAHA boundary: any code, the WAHA dashboard/Swagger, or the shared API key can still write, and session-level settings like noweb.markOnline (seed prod session ran markOnline:true, client.py:219-221) make WAHA itself emit presence with no client call at all. P7 is left unverified and L3 only proves zero writes after 24h on the real number. The simple structural guarantee is to give the product no send capability and put a deny rule for send/seen/presence routes in front of this instance, set markOnline false and verify it on a throwaway number first.

Over-built for D46: the full policy schema (allowlist, per_min/hour/day, jitter, warmup, read_receipts, presence, on_warning) and pacing/kill-switch gaps 7-8 serve live sends that D46 explicitly excludes. The actual requirement for this slice is one bit, send disabled and fail-closed, plus receive; the rest is inherited habit from the anti-ban research and can land with the first live-reply slice, when the agents team's real needs are also known. Putting S1 (seed-wide schema, keeper, KB) ahead of the first scheduling job delays the owner's evaluation.

The no-send guarantee rests on a wrapper around WahaClient, but the plan never says how it is injected: the seed inbox router mounted 'exactly as Monica' still exposes a POST send route (whatsapp_inbox_router.py:247-310) and the connections router builds clients itself, so any path that constructs a raw WahaClient bypasses C1. S1 must specify the injection seam (factory returns only the policy-wrapped client, no public raw constructor) and a test that every router in the mounted set cannot reach an unwrapped send, or the send routes must simply not be mounted for the Assistant. As written, L3 'zero sends' is an observation, not a guarantee.

The LGPD question (gap 9, S5) is gated at 'go-live' but storing begins at L1 pairing, and the session config defaults can set fullSync which backfills the whole history of a personal number (client.py:239-263), sending every old third-party chat through classification and shadow-reply LLM calls. The legal answer and a decision on history backfill (off, or a cutoff date) should gate pairing, not live replies, and the cost cap should be sized for the backfill case.

_session_config always sets noweb fullSync=True (client.py:239-272), so pairing the personal number backfills the entire chat history. The plan does not say whether backfilled messages fire on_message: if they do, S3 runs an LLM classification plus shadow reply on thousands of old third-party messages (cost burst, a polluted eval set, and L1's '10 s' meaningless); if not, the eval set misses history. Needs an explicit rule (live-only via timestamp/event type) and a cost cap proven before pairing.

A shadow-reply row for every inbound message multiplies LLM cost and stored text about third parties while the stated first question is only 'is this scheduling or not'. Generating the shadow reply only for scheduling-positive messages (or in a later slice) keeps the evaluation set intact and halves the exposure; the labelling web page (S4) is also replaceable at first by an export or SQL view to label against.

S3 consumes on_message without stating filters. notify_message also fires for the app's own outbound (from_me) messages and for groups/status, and the personal line receives group traffic. The classifier and shadow-reply rows need a defined input contract (inbound-only, 1:1 vs group, media/no-text handling, dedup on WAHA redelivery by message id) or the evaluation set is unusable and shadow replies get generated to the owner's own messages.

S6 depends on the agents team's Julia entry landing first, coupling the owner's personal line to another team's deploy order. The instance entry is independent per number; the dependency is only a file-merge conflict, so it should be a rebase note, not a slice dependency.

The slice plan has no one-line rollback and an unsafe ordering. S1 changes the shared WahaClient path and adds a keeper that refuses instances without an explicit send field, which can break the live Julia line unless existing entries and a default land in the same commit; this is not sequenced. Also nothing documents undoing a pairing (log out the linked device from the phone, app_enabled=false halts receive and send) or the revert order if S6 deployed before S1 behaviour is proven.

L3 and L4 are not testable as specified. 'WAHA outbound log shows 0 sends/seen/presence' assumes such a log exists and that WAHA NOWEB never emits presence or receipts itself (P7 is unverified); verify P7 against the live container before building. L4 (50 labels for precision/recall) has no definition of 'scheduling', no labelling protocol (agree/disagree anchors on the model's answer; blind labels are better) and no guarantee of enough positive examples for recall.

Over-built for the first question: producing a shadow reply row for every message, including non-scheduling ones, adds LLM cost and an undefined reply policy, while D46's first need is only the scheduling classification. Consider gating shadow replies behind is_scheduling or a later slice, and check P9 (per-day cost cap) before S3 since the plan assumes it exists.

The 'nothing is sent' guarantee is a client-side wrapper around WahaClient (C1), but writes can reach WAHA by any other path: the dev waha MCP (waha_message_send_text), any other container holding the WAHA key/URL, the WAHA dashboard/Swagger, and the inbox router's own POST send route (whatsapp_inbox_router.py:252-281) that S2 mounts 'exactly as Monica'. The only fail-closed guarantee is at the WAHA edge (a reverse proxy or network rule on the assistant instance denying /api/send*, /sendSeen, presence, reactions), and the plan never puts it there; L3 'zero sends' is then only an observation, not a prevention.

P7 is not just unverified, the code suggests it is true: the repo documents NOWEB config noweb.markOnline (client.py:219, test_client_webhook_merge.py:169-216) and a shared prod session ran markOnline:true; _session_config() does not set it, so WAHA's own default applies. If markOnline defaults to true the line shows 'online' to every contact whatever the policy says, so 'presence: 0' in L3 is unachievable or unprovable as written; the plan must set markOnline:false explicitly on the assistant session and prove it before pairing, not treat it as a policy field.

The first pairing is the highest-risk event and the plan has no control over it: _session_config forces store.fullSync=true, which backfills the owner's whole chat history on QR scan (client.py:263, docstring). Under D46 'store everything' that means years of third-party chats and groups landing at once, and if on_message / the shadow loop fires per stored message it classifies and drafts replies for the entire backlog, spiking LLM cost and bursting WAHA/LLM calls on a fresh personal number. Decide fullSync (likely false for a forward-only evaluation), group handling and backlog exclusion before S2/S3.

Ordering is wrong on privacy: S5 (LGPD) is gated only 'before go-live', but S3 sends every inbound third-party message, including groups and media captions, to an external LLM provider from the first day of pairing, and persists it on a NoctusAI server. The owner asked only for 'is this scheduling or not', so the per-message shadow-reply row (C3) is over-built for the first job and enlarges that exposure; ship classification only first, and make S5 a precondition of pairing, not of go-live.

on_message fires for outbound messages too (whatsapp_inbox_router.py:48, the send route calls notify_message with from_me=True), and fromMe messages the owner types on their phone also arrive via webhook. The plan says 'for each inbound message' but never specifies filtering from_me, so the owner's own messages and any UI-sent message would be classified and answered, polluting the evaluation set and potentially creating a reply loop once live replies exist. Add an explicit from_me/direction filter and test it.

The line policy design (C1) is over-built for the three-line, two-team ask and wrongly shaped: it ships pacing, allowlist, warmup and on_warning fields for sends that are disabled, and puts the enforcing wrapper in the seed while enforcement for the other teams' lines relies on them calling it. The business line is already warm and inbound-only; changing its config schema (a required explicit 'send' field keeper) lands on a live line owned by another team, in the same file S6 edits. Ship only send:disabled plus edge enforcement now, and let pacing arrive with the first live-send slice.

Gap 8 (kill switch on warnings) rests on P8, event names FIRST/SECOND_WARNING and 463/475 taken from a research doc, not from WAHA docs or code, so the keeper and halt logic would be built against guessed signals. Verify the actual WAHA session.status/engine events (or accept 'only observable symptom is session FAILED/STOPPED') before specifying on_warning:halt; also note recover_session/restart_session loops in client.py can re-pair automatically and must be disabled for this line.

C3/C4 and slices S3/S4 allocate the classification store, shadow-reply store and labelling page as new per-product tables and a bespoke page, but the seed already ships these organs: noctusai_lib/domain/ai/outputs.py (ai_outputs with kind classification|narrative, label, confidence, model_version, prompt_version, metadata), seed/framework/backend/noctusai_seed/ai_feedback_router.py (per-output rating, opt-in via standard_routers) and the AIFeedbackButtons/useAIFeedback organs in seed/lib/frontend/src/design-system/ai/. Allocate the classifier row to ai_outputs(kind=classification), the shadow reply to ai_outputs(kind=narrative) and the owner's agree/disagree to ai_feedback, extending via seam only for what is missing (latency/cost, an append-only event, a labelling queue view); otherwise this is the per-product re-implementation the organ-consumption rule forbids, and the evaluation would not be reusable by the agents team's lines.

C1 keys the line policy by product (<PRODUCT>_WAHA_LINE_POLICY next to <PRODUCT>_WAHA_BASE_URL, as waha_instance.py:181-183 renders), but the variation axis is the line (WAHA instance), and the agents team's two lines (Julia business line + the future third line) would both sit under product agents and collide on one key; waha_instance.py validation only rejects duplicate instance names, not two instances per product. Key the policy, base URL and session by instance name and have the wrapper resolve policy from the connection's instance, so the variant matrix is line x policy, not product x policy, before the agents team consumes it.

S3 bundles the first job (is-this-scheduling classification, L2/L4) with shadow-reply generation, i.e. executing the request as an agent turn inside products/assistant/backend/app/shadow, while the agents product already owns an LLM agent runtime and eval machinery (products/agents/backend runtime/llm_runtime, studio eval mechanism); the plan records no allocation decision for where 'execute the request' lives. Split S3 so the classifier and its labelled evaluation land first, and make the shadow reply a later slice whose home (assistant-local vs a capability interface to the agents runtime, link not merge) is decided explicitly, so a second agent runtime is not grown by default.

C2 creates products/assistant without recording why the function set (personal calendar/scheduling, AI-assisted, user-scoped) is not allocated to the existing but inactive products/daily-life, whose README already claims calendar events and AI assistance, or to monica which already mounts the seed WhatsApp routers. A one-line allocation rationale (new product vs extend daily-life vs monica module) should be in the Phase 0 addendum so the owner decides it rather than it being implied by the scaffold slice.

P7 is false: WAHA NOWEB sends an online presence on session start by default (noweb.markOnline, 'default true' per waha.devlike.pro/docs/engines/noweb), and the seed start_session/_session_config (client.py:237-270) never sets it, while _merged_session_config preserves whatever exists. So the owner's personal number broadcasts presence the moment it pairs, a WhatsApp write no app-side wrapper can see or refuse. The line policy must be applied in the session config itself (markOnline=false, set and verified via GET /api/sessions) before the QR scan, and L3 must assert it.

C1 does not name where the wrapper is injected: the inbox router's send_message route (whatsapp_inbox_router.py:247, gated only by app_enabled), mark_read, the @lid resolver client and the connections router all build clients via waha_client_factory, which defaults to the raw get_whatsapp_client, and Monica (the template C2 copies) takes that default. Enforcement must be by construction in the seed factory/client (policy resolved per connection, refuse on missing policy), not a wrapper a product must remember to pass, with a test that every route mounted with defaults refuses a send on a send=disabled line.

'Zero writes' is only enforced inside the product: the instance's WAHA API key and its dashboard + Swagger (enabled with a password in compose.waha.yml:17-20) can send, mark seen or set presence directly, and WAHA Core has no read-only key. For the personal line, disable the dashboard/Swagger on that instance, keep the API key out of every MCP/n8n/agent env, and make L3 a WAHA-side proof (session config + WAHA's own events over 24h) rather than the wrapper's refusal log.

S5 (LGPD) has no edge into S6 (deploy), so the line can go live before the legal answer the plan itself says is required; and the seed start config sets fullSync=true, so a fresh pairing backfills the owner's entire personal history (third parties, groups, likely health/minors data) and C3 then sends that content to an external LLM provider (international transfer, LGPD art. 33). Make S5 a hard dependency of S6, and before pairing decide purpose limitation (inbound-from-pairing-forward only, fullSync=false, no backfill route), retention/deletion, sensitive-category handling and the LLM provider's no-retention terms.

The inbound webhook verifies HMAC only when webhook_hmac_secret is passed (webhook_endpoint bypass_when_unset=True, whatsapp_inbox_router.py:399-406), and the plan's C2 mount does not pass it although the WAHA instance signs with WAHA_<NAME>_HMAC_SECRET. On a line whose content feeds an LLM and an evaluation set, a leaked path token lets anyone inject fabricated messages; the assistant mount should require the secret and refuse to start in prod without it.

Access tier is declared only for the labelling page; the stored chat, classification and shadow-reply tables hold the owner's private conversations and must declare org tier with no browser PostgREST grant beyond the owner's org, and service-role/platform-admin reads of this product's data should be audited or excluded. Separately, once the 'execute the actual request' slice gives the loop tools, any contact can steer the owner's calendar by prompt injection, so that slice needs an agents-security review before it is built, not after.

The 'nothing is written to WhatsApp' guarantee cannot come from a client-side wrapper, because the session config is a WAHA-side write path. WahaClient.start_session/restart_session send _session_config() (client.py:237-270, 646-690) with no noweb.markOnline, so WAHA falls back to its own default (the in-code note at client.py:219 records a prod session running markOnline:true): the line then shows the owner as online and his phone stops getting notifications, and fullSync:true pulls his whole chat history. The line policy must be written into the session config (_session_config and _merged_session_config, keyed by line), and L3 must check GET /api/sessions/default config, not only send counts.

C1's wrapper is opt-in, so it does not cover every write. Products build clients through get_whatsapp_client and also directly (seed finance reminders channel.py:142 does WahaClient(rec.base_url, ...)), and a borrower product sharing the same session reads its own env. Put the refusal at the one choke point every request passes, WahaClient._request, resolved by base_url+session, with a keeper that bans direct WahaClient construction outside the seed; or state why the factory alone is enough.

Keying the policy as a per-product env JSON (<PRODUCT>_WAHA_LINE_POLICY) breaks for three lines and two teams. One product can hold several lines (the agents team's business line plus the third line), and the per-line state already lives in the org-scoped connection row (app_enabled, session_role; connection_store.py:76-108). Key the policy by WAHA instance/session, keep the fleet file as the platform-owned ceiling an org admin cannot raise, model app_enabled plus send mode as one receive x send line state with transition events (EOA E1), and name the context-map relation the agents team consumes (open-host/shared kernel).

C3 hangs the shadow loop on on_message, which runs inline in the webhook request and swallows every exception (ingest.py:337-345, inbox router :47). An LLM classify call plus a reply call per message there slows the webhook, and any failure leaves a message with no row and only a log line, so L2 ('every inbound message has a classification row') cannot be proven. Have on_message only append a pending intake row in the same transaction, process it with a worker that records an outcome enum (classified/failed/skipped_budget), and filter from_me, since on_message also fires on outbound sends.

The evaluation design records a classification only once, on arrival. Nothing re-runs the stored messages through a new prompt or model version, so after the first prompt change the 50+ owner labels can no longer compare versions. Make classifications unique on (message_id, prompt_version, model), add a replay job over the stored corpus, and store the owner's labels as their own append-only label events (relabels allowed) that are independent of any classification row.

The LGPD question (S5) is ordered as 'before go-live', but storing third parties' messages starts at pairing (L0/L1), and fullSync backfills the owner's full history into the shared pooled DB. S6 (fleet entry + deploy) should depend on S5, and the storage tier (who reads it: org admin vs platform admins, retention, purge) should be stated before the QR scan.

S3 generates a shadow reply for every inbound message, including groups and non-scheduling chatter, before the classifier is measured, which doubles LLM spend for little evaluation value. Run the classifier first and gate shadow-reply generation on is_scheduling (or on owner labels). P9 (a per-day cost cap) is unverified; when the cap is hit, write an explicit skipped_budget outcome rather than dropping silently.

decision: Zero writes enforced in three layers (edge deny proxy on the assistant WAHA instance with dashboard/Swagger off; Assistant mounts no send/read/backfill routes; seed WahaClient._request choke point keyed by line + keeper banning raw construction). Session config markOnline=false, fullSync=false, re-pair loops off, checked before QR. Policy v1 = send disabled|enabled + session flags, keyed per instance; line state on the connection row with events. Input contract (inbound, 1:1, exclusion list, text-only, dedup, forward-only) before S3; on_message appends intake rows, worker classifies with outcome enum; reuse ai_outputs/ai_feedback organs; blind stratified labelling. S3 = classification only; shadow reply later, only for is_scheduling, after agents-security. LGPD artefacts gate the QR scan. HMAC required on the webhook.
biggest_risk: The first QR scan of the owner's real number under today's seed defaults: WAHA shows online and backfills the full history to an external LLM; irreversible WhatsApp write and LGPD exposure no app wrapper can undo.
first_step: Bring up a throwaway-number WAHA instance with markOnline=false, fullSync=false, edge deny proxy, dashboard off; prove session config, 24h zero presence/seen/sends (P7) and the real session-state events (P8). In parallel, legal-advisor drafts the S5 artefacts.
